title: Engine permanently hangs (main thread infinite loop in SDL joystick code) when a GameSir T4n controller disconnects on Windows
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.stable.official [5b4e0cb0f]

### System information

Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated GPU - 20 CPU threads

### Issue description

When a **GameSir T4n Life** controller (VID 0x3537, PID 0x1040, XInput mode, 2.4GHz USB dongle) is disconnected — either by unplugging the dongle or powering off the pad — the engine **permanently freezes**: the window stops responding and must be killed via Task Manager. Audio keeps playing (audio thread alive). This happens in exported games AND in the editor itself, on any project (project-independent).

Other controllers (Xbox, etc.) disconnect cleanly on the same machine. This looks like the same class of bug as #112658 (8BitDo Ultimate 2 lockup on disconnect), which was closed without a root cause. I captured **two full memory dumps of the hung process, ~10 seconds apart**, and analyzed them with WinDbg:

**Main thread (thread 0) — identical stack in both dumps, instruction pointer actively executing (busy loop, not a blocked syscall):**

```
Child-SP          RetAddr               Call Site
0000007f`7fffeae0 00007ff6`2ede57c1     Godot_v4_7_stable_win64+0x1555660
0000007f`7fffeba0 00007ff6`2ede58cd     Godot_v4_7_stable_win64+0x15557c1
0000007f`7fffec20 00007ff6`2ed387e5     Godot_v4_7_stable_win64+0x15558cd
0000007f`7fffece0 00007ff6`2ede5b65     Godot_v4_7_stable_win64+0x14a87e5
0000007f`7fffed20 00007ff6`2edd81c5     Godot_v4_7_stable_win64+0x1555b65
0000007f`7fffedf0 00007ff6`2edd83ba     Godot_v4_7_stable_win64+0x15481c5
0000007f`7fffeec0 00007ff6`2ed3affa     Godot_v4_7_stable_win64+0x15483ba
0000007f`7fffefa0 00007ff6`2d8b82ed     Godot_v4_7_stable_win64+0x14aaffa
0000007f`7ffff1b0 00007ff6`2d892eec     Godot_v4_7_stable_win64+0x282ed
0000007f`7ffff260 00007ff6`2d8e2502     Godot_v4_7_stable_win64+0x2eec
0000007f`7ffff2a0 00007ff6`2d8e253e     Godot_v4_7_stable_win64+0x52502
...
kernel32!BaseThreadInitThunk / ntdll!RtlUserThreadStart
```
(module base 0x7ff62d890000; offsets are absolute minus base, from the official 4.7-stable win64 binary)

Additional findings:

- The `SDL_joystick` thread exists and is alive (caught around `ntdll!RtlReleaseSRWLockExclusive` returning into godot SDL code), so this involves the SDL joystick driver added in 4.5.
- Disassembly of the innermost frames shows loops iterating a joystick's axes/buttons/hats arrays (counts at struct offsets +0x60/+0x70/+0x80, array ptr at +0x88) — consistent with SDL's "send final/zero events on removal" path — and a **linked-list walk** (`mov rax,[rax+0x158]; cmp [rax],ebx; jne` loop) that matches SDL's joystick-list lookup by instance ID. The identical stack 10 s apart suggests that lookup/iteration never terminates (list corrupted or made circular during removal).
- A `--verbose` log shows nothing at the moment of the hang — the freeze happens inside native code before any disconnect message is printed, and `Input.joy_connection_changed` never reaches script.
- The controller is a composite device exposing several HID interfaces simultaneously (XInput gamepad `IG_01` + HID keyboard + consumer control), which may be why it triggers the removal path bug while ordinary pads don't.

I still have both .dmp files (1.7 GB each) and can share them or run further WinDbg commands on request.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, connect a GameSir T4n (XInput mode, 2.4G dongle).
2. Open any project in the editor, or run any game.
3. Unplug the dongle (or power off the pad).
4. Engine hangs permanently (window "Not Responding", audio continues).

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A — reproducible with the editor itself / empty project.
